subject_line: From Kitchens at Night to After Party
email_body:
Dear Dean,

I've been following the path from your pamphlet Kitchens at Night to your Picador debut After Party, and congratulations on the Pigott Poetry Prize at Listowel and on the residency at UCC this year.

I'd love to ask how the poems of Kitchens at Night carried over into After Party: which ones stayed, which changed, and what the full collection let you do that a pamphlet couldn't.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. Each portrait is built from a few written questions that you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication.

Would you be open to taking part? No pressure either way.

Best regards,
The Author Ledger
hook_note: Tipperary-born poet; debut After Party (Picador 2025) won Pigott Poetry Prize; pamphlet Kitchens at Night (2022); 2026 Arts Council Writer in Residence at UCC (ucc.ie pages). Email seen in search result from UCC creative writing staff page.

email_body:
Dear Kunal,

I came across Satrangi Dastarkhwan, your Hindi book with Rajkamal Prakashan that won Best Printed Book of the Year (Indian Languages) at the Publishing Next awards, and it seemed of a piece with your work co-editing On Eating, the multilingual journal of food.

I'd be curious what writing about food in Hindi opened up for you, compared with your criticism in English on music, song-text and film.

subject_line: The two women at the centre of The Remains of the Body
email_body:
Dear Saikat,

I was interested to read that The Remains of the Body, published by Vintage as Penguin Random House India's Pride Month selection in 2024, is set on a campus and seen through the eyes of two female characters.

I'd like to ask why you chose to tell this campus story through those two women, and how years of teaching in India and abroad found their way into the fiction.

subject_line: After We Were Young, Make Strange
email_body:
Dear Niamh,

I've been reading about the run from This Happy, which won the Rooney Prize in 2021, through We Were Young in 2022 to your third novel, Make Strange, due this June.

I'd love to ask what changed in how you approached a novel by the third time, and whether the title Make Strange describes something you were trying to do on the page.

subject_line: A History of Running Away in German
email_body:
Dear Paula,

I noticed that A History of Running Away, first published by John Murray in 2017, appeared in German translation in 2022, five years after its English release and a few years after Generation.

I'd be interested to hear what it was like to see the novel return in another language that much later, and whether running UCD's creative writing programme has changed how you look back on those two books.
